title: Avalanche Staking - Open App
meta_description: avalanche staking starts in Core: connect a compatible wallet, review P-Chain delegation or validation, and open the official app.
hero_h2: Delegate AVAX or validate through Core
hero_lead: avalanche staking starts in Core Stake, where AVAX holders can delegate to a validator or validate with their own node after reviewing P-Chain requirements, lock terms, and rewards.
what_is: Core Stake is the Core web destination for delegating AVAX or validating on Avalanche, with staking activity handled through the P-Chain. The Avalanche Builder Hub documents the minimums, lock terms, and reward rules.

how.d: Open Core Stake and connect a Core-compatible wallet before reviewing balances and chain location.
If your AVAX is on the C-Chain, use the cross-chain transfer flow so it is available for staking.
Delegate at least 25 AVAX to an active validator, or validate with a prepared node and at least 2,000 AVAX.
Check validator, amount, reward address, and term before signing; confirmed staking parameters cannot be changed early.

points.p: Core Stake supports validation, delegation, and X/P/C cross-chain transfers directly in Core web, as described in Core support.
Staking uses AVAX on the Platform Chain, not the C-Chain DeFi environment, so chain placement matters before signing.
Mainnet staking terms run from 2 weeks to 1 year, and rewards are paid at the end if protocol conditions are met.

faq.q: What is avalanche staking in Core?
faq.a: It is the Core web flow for placing AVAX on the P-Chain as a delegator or validator, helping secure Avalanche through a self-custody wallet workflow.

faq.q: What are the avalanche staking minimums?
faq.a: Avalanche mainnet requires at least 25 AVAX to delegate and 2,000 AVAX to validate, according to the official staking parameters.

faq.q: Can avalanche staking be withdrawn early?
faq.a: No. Once a staking transaction is confirmed, the amount, validator, reward address, and term cannot be changed until the selected period ends.

faq.q: Is avalanche staking done on the C-Chain?
faq.a: No. Staking occurs on the P-Chain; Core can help move AVAX between the C-Chain, P-Chain, and X-Chain before you stake.
Avalanche documentation states there is no protocol slashing, but a validator that fails uptime requirements can result in zero rewards for that staking period.

footer_note: Not the official app; verify core.app before connecting a wallet. Educational only, not financial advice.
